system_overview: This specification models a high-level consensus algorithm based on voting with ballots. A set of acceptors cooperatively choose a value by casting votes in numbered ballot rounds. A value is chosen when a quorum of acceptors all vote for the same value in the same ballot. The algorithm refines the abstract consensus specification and serves as the foundation for more concrete Paxos variants.
actors_and_components: The system consists of acceptors that cast votes in ballots. A quorum is defined as any set of acceptors such that any two quorums have a non-empty intersection. There are no explicit leader or proposer processes; the algorithm specifies only what actions acceptors may take.
state_variables: The system tracks two arrays indexed by acceptor: (1) The set of votes cast by each acceptor, where each vote is a pair of a ballot number and a value. (2) The highest ballot number in which each acceptor has participated (or negative one if it has not yet participated). An acceptor cannot vote in any ballot lower than its recorded maximum.
initial_state: Every acceptor has cast no votes (empty vote set). Every acceptor's maximum ballot is negative one (has not participated in any ballot).
actions: Each acceptor can perform two actions in each step, nondeterministically choosing a ballot number: (1) Increase maximum ballot: if the chosen ballot exceeds the acceptor's current maximum ballot, update the maximum to the chosen ballot. This prevents the acceptor from voting in lower-numbered ballots. (2) Vote for a value: if the chosen ballot is at least the acceptor's current maximum ballot, the acceptor has not already voted in that ballot, all other acceptors that voted in that ballot voted for the same value, and the value is safe at that ballot number, then the acceptor casts a vote for that value and updates its maximum ballot. Safety at a ballot is defined recursively: a value is safe at ballot zero unconditionally; at higher ballots, it is safe if there exists a quorum where all members have participated at or above that ballot, and either no member voted in any ballot between some cutoff and the current ballot, or the value was itself safe at the cutoff ballot and all votes at the cutoff were for the same value.
safety_properties: Four invariants are maintained: (1) Type correctness for votes and maximum ballots. (2) An acceptor's maximum ballot is at least as large as the ballot of any vote it has cast. (3) If an acceptor has voted in a ballot, it has not voted in any ballot between that vote's ballot and its maximum ballot. (4) Every vote cast is for a value that is safe at the vote's ballot number. Together these ensure the key safety property: the set of chosen values always has cardinality at most one. The specification formally refines the abstract consensus specification.
liveness_properties: A liveness specification adds fairness conditions ensuring that if a quorum of acceptors are responsive and a ballot is sufficiently stable, then eventually some value is chosen.
model_bounds: Constants include the set of choosable values, the set of acceptors, and the set of quorums. Ballot numbers are natural numbers. For model checking, typical values are two values, three acceptors, and all subsets of size two or more as quorums, with ballots restricted to zero through two.
additional_assumptions: The specification uses PlusCal for the algorithm, translated to TLA+. It imports the abstract consensus specification and proves refinement: the set of values for which a quorum has unanimously voted in some ballot equals the chosen set of the consensus specification. The recursive safety definition uses a function definition rather than recursive operator definition because the TLAPS proof system does not support the latter. The specification includes formal proofs of all invariants and the refinement theorem, checked by TLAPS. Quorums must satisfy the intersection property: any two quorums share at least one acceptor.
